text:
incident-bot: 🚨 PagerDuty: p99 latency alert fired for service=runtime-inference, region=ap-southeast-1, metric=p99_latency_ms, value=1350ms, threshold=1000ms. Policy: p99-latency-prod. Page sent to #eng-oncall and rotation.
pagerduty: PagerDuty: Alert INC-8421 created and routed to rotation -> michael (primary).
michael: ack INC-8421. I'm looking. grabbing traces and recent deploys.
michael: quick note: saw a spike at 16:17 UTC, spike coincides with a batch of large payloads (ctx_len ~ 4600) and a cluster of kvcache misses.
sara: @michael can you confirm whether this is p95 or p99 only? Customer impact?
michael: p95 is elevated but within SLO; p99 is the one melting. Affected routes: /v1/generate (model: redwood-7b-quant).
alan: adding runbook link: <https://runbook.internal/realtime/kv-thrash>
alan: also see sidecar logs showing evictions: `kvcache_evictions_total` jumped x10 at 16:16 UTC. Could be GC churn + new quantized model kernel.
michael: running `kubectl top pods -n inference | grep runtime` — memory stable but CPU on some pods hit 95%. suspect hotkey + continuous batching causing compute starvation.
ops-bot: autoscaler: scaled down group inference-apac-2 from 8 -> 5 at 16:12 UTC due to scheduled downscale window.
nina: on-call hand: I'm @nina taking next 20min to help — pls ping if you need escalation to pd-esc.
sara: pinging Customer Success: any live customer reports?
ops-bot: CS: no public tickets yet. Two customers with reserved Dedicated capacity flagged higher latency in their dashboards.
michael: mitigation plan: 1) temporarily increase min replicas for inference-apac-2 to 8, 2) enable fallback routing to eu-west for affected routes, 3) deploy a small kvcache size bump config.
alan: command to bump min replicas: ```sh
kubectl scale deployment/inference-runtime-apac-2 --replicas=8 -n inference
```
michael: executing scale now.
sara: @michael please post rollout id and timeline.
michael: scaled -> replicas=8. Pods scheduling, new pods becoming ready (3/3 containers ready).
ops-bot: autoscaler suspension: paused horizontal-autoscaler for inference-apac-2 until manual resume.
nina: I'm routing 10% of traffic for this customer cohort to eu-west as a soft fallback. Using routing rule id r-7402.
michael: added a short-lived canaryroute redirect: `traffic-weight: apac:90 eu:10` for /v1/generate.
alan: also increased kvcache capacity per-pod from 128MB -> 192MB via configmap patch: ```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  kvcache_max_bytes: "201326592"
```
sara: good. any quick checks for error rates?
michael: 500s not increased, just latency; logs show repeated `kv-miss` plus `batch-queue-delay` spikes.
ops-bot: metric update (16:24 UTC): p99 dropped from 1350ms -> 980ms after scale + routing change. p95 steady ~220ms.
nina: customers on dedicated still blipping — their traffic is pinned to apac-2 and can't follow fallback. contacting solutions-eng to message CS.
sara: tagging @customer-success to prep a short note: "We observed elevated tail latency in APAC; mitigation applied; Dedicated customers may still see intermittent latency while we finalize config."
michael: next steps: keep autoscaler paused, monitor p99 for 15m, if stable resume normal autoscale and revert routing. If it flaps again, escalate to PD-ENG for kernel rollback.
alan: ETA to stabilize looks ~10-15m, pods warm KV caches during warmup so expect p99 to tick down gradually.
nina: taking over active watch. @michael handing off since you need to join standup. I'll update every 5m or on any regression.
michael: thanks — handing off. cc: @pagerduty for escalation if p99 > 1200ms again.
ops-bot: note: suspended autoscaler will auto-resume at 17:00 UTC if not manually resumed.
sara: please capture all commands and timeline in the incident doc (link below) once stable.
nina: will do. current p99=940ms (16:31 UTC). monitoring. :thumbsup: 
incident-bot: Reminder: If alert re-triggers within 10m, automatic escalation to PD-ENG will occur.
ops-bot: resume scheduled autoscaler at 16:48 UTC (manual).
nina: resuming autoscaler now.
op-bot: autoscaler resumed. p99 steady 920ms.
sara: closing check: did we identify root cause? short answer: combination of downscale window + kvcache evictions causing compute hotpath bursts at tail. Recommend: adjust scale schedules and increase kvcache headroom.
alan: filing follow-up action items: 1) change downscale policy for apac to avoid cross-region risk windows, 2) add kvcache metric alert for eviction rate, 3) run a load replay to validate.
nina: updating the incident doc and marking this thread resolved.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: INC-8421 acknowledged and resolved by nina.
